I re-verified all seven actionable phase-16 findings as fixed in this source: constructor rustdoc with a compiled no_run example and the DEVELOPMENT.md entry-point list (access_policies.rs:135-151, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:83), the shared crate::redaction::redacted_debug! replacing the duplicated local macro, required fixture `reason` fields enforced at tools/portkey-access.mjs:74 plus the contract-description assertions at tools/test_portkey_access.py:34-36, invalid-identifier coverage extended to update and delete (portkey_access_contracts.rs:242-260), the whitespace guard extended to model-fixtures.json/operations.json, exact sorted header-set assertions for all five requests (lines 149-161), and deduplicated scope_evidence. I also re-checked the contract field-by-field against contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/contract.json: routes, Portkey-Key scheme, name 1..64, nullable description max 256, subjects/targets minItems 1, version minimum 1, the twelve query parameters with maxLength 36/36/100/64/255 and minimum-0 paging (workspace_id correctly left unbounded because the schema declares no maximum), RFC3339 timestamps, MCP tools required versus provider models optional, ALL-or-nonempty-list selectors, and the exact create effect-inference sentence at contract.json:21 — all implemented faithfully, with response structs covering every declared AccessPolicy/AccessPolicyListItem field and keeping effect/kind/status/target variants open. Residual findings are governance, documentation and style gaps: incomplete phase-17 scope_evidence (a third recurrence of the same class), no executed guard that publication/tag/terminal-CI receipts exist before phase 17 is marked complete, a private-material receipt bound to the pre-release HEAD with a checker that never compares headCommit to actual HEAD, the still-unformatted long test binding deferred from phase 16, and stale release-procedure prose. None is a blocker or high.

findings.description: Phase 17's scope_evidence omits this phase's own executed evidence and several of its own authored artifacts. It lists only docs/checks/phase-17-release-package-1.89.0.json and -1.99.0.json, while docs/checks/phase-17.json (the gate receipt), the nine docs/checks/phase-17-rust-*.json child reports, docs/checks/phase-17-candidate.json, docs/checks/phase-17-dependencies.json and docs/checks/phase-17-private-material.json are absent; docs/checks/phase-17-access-live.json appears only under live_evidence. It also omits authored inputs this phase changed: crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml (the 0.2.0 -> 0.2.1 bump at line 3), docs/RELEASE.md, docs/STABILITY.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (the new entry-point list at line 83), and the retargeted immutable-runtime guard at tools/test_release_020.py:28-32. This is the third recurrence of the same finding class after phase 15 (docs/phase-status.json:3316-3321) and phase 16 (docs/reviews/phase-16-attempt-01.json finding 5, recorded implemented at docs/phase-status.json:3447-3452), so the ledger that a reader uses to locate this phase's proof is still incomplete even though the duplication part of that finding was fixed.
findings.required_fix: Extend phase 17 scope_evidence with docs/checks/phase-17.json, the nine phase-17-rust-*.json reports, phase-17-candidate.json, phase-17-dependencies.json, phase-17-private-material.json, phase-17-access-live.json, crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml, docs/RELEASE.md, docs/STABILITY.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and tools/test_release_020.py, and add an assertion (tools/test_portkey_access.py or tools/test_ci.py) that every docs/checks/phase-17*.json report referenced by commands_for(17) appears in the phase's scope_evidence.

findings.description: The publication preconditions for completing this phase exist only as prose. delivery.advance_requires lists "verified registry 0.2.1", "verified immutable v0.2.1 source tag" and "terminal exact 47-job CI run", but nothing executed enforces them: tools/review_phase.py:177-190 advances the active phase to complete on an accepted >=9 review plus check_evidence alone, and tools/test_portkey_access.py:111-119 validates docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.1.json only `if path.exists()`. tools/test_ci.py:291-297 inspects the last phase carrying a registry_publication key, and phase 17 has no such key, so a phase-17 completion with no publication at all would pass every check. Because the accepted review is by design taken before publication (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:127), this review cannot itself supply that evidence, and no later gate re-checks it. Phase 8 and phase 92 by contrast recorded explicit remote-gate conditions (docs/phase-status.json:3154-3158).
findings.required_fix: Add an executed assertion (tools/test_portkey_access.py or tools/test_ci.py) that when phase 17 status is "complete" the receipts docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.1.json, docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.1.json and a terminal 47-job CI observation must all exist, bind releaseCommit 80baf80f0f6d90f9b382e8895083ca30fa5e8997 and the 1.99.0 archive digest 624f97bbc3fba604e0317d68c04a8ef88b35c104d504b44e1a235f38bd01d0d4, and record a registry_publication block for 0.2.1 so tools/test_ci.py:291-315 applies.

findings.description: The final credential scan for this release is bound to a pre-release commit and the re-verification path cannot detect that. docs/checks/phase-17-private-material.json:3-6 was produced at 22:35:22 with headCommit a9b2e2658c72c0b86b3953e0046d5ba9fbc9611c, whereas the qualified release commit is 80baf80f0f6d90f9b382e8895083ca30fa5e8997 (docs/checks/phase-17-release-package-1.99.0.json:8). The gate's last command is `--check` against that receipt, and check_receipt only re-derives sourceSha256 and the published-candidate fingerprints (lines 168-173) while merely format-validating headCommit at line 174; it never compares it to `git rev-parse HEAD`. headCommit is what drives the existingTenantIdentifier "alreadyPresentInHead" exemption (lines 110-121), so a receipt whose HEAD does not match the delivered commit leaves that exemption computed against an arbitrary tree. For this receipt the direction is conservative (newOrChangedFilesCount 0 against an older HEAD), and the published-source scan reports zero matches, so no secret exposure is indicated; the gap is that the phase-8 advisory requiring the selected-value scan to be refreshed after the final delivery records (docs/phase-status.json:743-749) is not satisfied for the release commit and cannot be enforced.
findings.required_fix: Make check_receipt assert report["headCommit"] equals the current `git rev-parse HEAD`, and regenerate docs/checks/phase-17-private-material.json at the qualified release commit before publication so the receipt's head identity matches the delivered source.

findings.description: The rustfmt-unformatted long binding flagged as phase-16 finding 7 is unchanged: line 104 is still a single ~320-character statement written `let query:AccessPolicyListOptions=serde_json::from_value(json!({...})).unwrap();` with no spaces around `:` or `=`, which is precisely why rustfmt silently skips it and `cargo fmt --check` still passes (docs/checks/phase-17-rust-1.99.0-gateway.json shows fmt at exit 0). Lines 84-85 remain 200-300 character json! literals. docs/phase-status.json:3453-3458 records this as deferred "post_release_style_maintenance", so the deferral is disclosed, but the effect is that this file's layout is effectively unchecked by the formatter in a release phase, continuing a pattern earlier reviews raised in phases 3, 5, 15 and 16.
findings.required_fix: Split the binding at line 104 (and the literals at lines 84-85) into pre-bound json! values or multiple statements so rustfmt formats them, then re-run scripts/check-rust.py for the gateway feature on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 and refresh those child reports.

findings.description: The governing release procedure is only partly updated for this release. The header (lines 3-7) states the 0.2.1 workspace version and the receipt-conditional publication language, but the numbered procedure still describes only the 0.1.1/0.2.0 path: step 2 (line 72) names `tools/check_phase.py --phase 91` with no equivalent for `--phase 17`, and the publication-authorization paragraph at line 126 says "Maintainer authorization covers 0.1.1 and the subsequent 0.2.0 delivery" without extending it to 0.2.1, even though docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:3 is the document that authorizes 0.2.1 publication. The new candidate verifier scripts/check-access-release.py is not mentioned anywhere in docs/RELEASE.md, so a reader following the release document would not run it.
findings.required_fix: Add 0.2.1 to the publication-authorization paragraph, add a procedure step for `python3 tools/check_phase.py --phase 17` and for `python3 scripts/check-access-release.py --output docs/checks/phase-17-candidate.json`, and reference docs/ACCESS_POLICIES.md from the release document.

findings.description: The module-level PROTECTED tuple ("Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock", "LICENSE", "NOTICE", "crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml", "crates/scm-sdk/src", "crates/scm-sdk/examples") is never referenced by verify() or main(); it appears to be carried over from scripts/check-release-candidate.py, whose own PROTECTED is exercised by tools/test_release_020.py:52. The actual protected-input comparison in this script is driven by the archive member names at lines 59-78 and by the explicit four-path list at line 89. A dead constant that names the protection policy but does not implement it is misleading in a release-gating script.
findings.required_fix: Either delete the unused PROTECTED constant or use it to drive the protected-input comparison at scripts/check-access-release.py:59-91, and add a negative unit test that a modified protected input fails verification.

findings.description: The documented claim that both response-default modes produce identical data for this family (docs/ACCESS_POLICIES.md:25-27 and docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:86-87) is not asserted for the same payload. In the wire test, get() is the only call made with `.without_response_defaults()` (line 111, asserted against `detail` at lines 112-115), while create/list/update/delete run with None options, i.e. defaults enabled. No test decodes one response body under both modes and asserts equality, so the equivalence statement rests on the absence of declared defaults (tools/response_defaults.py --check still reports 23 bindings) rather than on a direct behavioral assertion.
findings.required_fix: Add an assertion that the same `detail` body round-trips byte-identically through get() both with default options and with `.without_response_defaults()`, and do the same for one AccessPolicyPage body.

findings.description: One client-side rule that is stricter than the pinned schema is not stated in the feature documentation. crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/gateway/access_policies.rs:101-106 rejects any subject whose id is exactly "ANY" when its type is "group", which contract.json:564-583 permits (id is an unconstrained string) and which is only justified by the upstream prose at contract.json:581. The deviation is recorded in the plan (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:60) and in the fixture rationale (contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/model-fixtures.json:344) and is exercised by portkey_access_contracts.rs:212-217, but docs/ACCESS_POLICIES.md:29-33 explains only the allow/ANY inference, so a caller reading the feature document cannot predict the group-ANY validation error.
findings.required_fix: State in docs/ACCESS_POLICIES.md that `ANY` is accepted only for user and agent subjects and that a group subject with id `ANY` is rejected before dispatch as a deliberate, prose-derived restriction.

findings.description: The two clean-archive proofs cannot have been produced consecutively at their recorded paths and no receipt records how they were produced. scripts/check-package.py:108-110 aborts when `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is non-empty, and docs/checks is not ignored (.gitignore lists only target/, /.local/ and credential patterns), so the 1.89.0 report written at 22:41:22 would have blocked the 1.99.0 run that completed at 22:47:44. docs/RELEASE.md:88-108 does document the correct pattern (run both with ignored .local/ output paths, then promote the proofs in a later evidence-only commit), so the plausible provenance is a promotion — but these two invocations are necessarily outside commands_for(17) (including them would self-dirty the gate), and nothing records the exact commands, ordering, original output paths or promotion step for this release.
findings.required_fix: Record a small provenance receipt alongside the two proofs (exact scripts/check-package.py invocations with --require-clean, original ignored output paths, ordering and the promotion commit), and have scripts/check-access-release.py verify that receipt so the clean-proof pair is as source-bound as the archives it certifies.

limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing. Every pass/fail claim rests on recorded reports (docs/checks/phase-17.json, the nine check-rust child reports, both release-package proofs, phase-17-candidate.json, phase-17-dependencies.json, phase-17-private-material.json, phase-17-access-live.json and phase-08-live-attempt-13.json), whose command lists, source digests and per-command stdout/stderr I inspected; I could not re-run cargo, node, ajv, cargo-audit or the Python suite.

I had no git access in this session, so I could not independently confirm that HEAD is 80baf80f0f6d90f9b382e8895083ca30fa5e8997, that the tree is clean, or the exact commit at which each proof ran; the clean-proof sequencing finding is derived from scripts/check-package.py:108-110 plus .gitignore and the recorded checkedAt timestamps rather than from observed repository state.

I did not read any credential or tenant-registration material, so the not_attempted live classification (no compatible Portkey control-plane endpoint/key in the retained registration) and the private-material scan's zero selected-value matches are taken at face value from their sanitized receipts.

Publication is not assessed because it has not occurred: there is no docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.1.json, no docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.1.json and no terminal 47-job CI observation for this source. The plan places this review before publication, so those remain outstanding delivery obligations rather than review evidence, and docs/phase-status.json still shows phase 17 in_progress with delivery.status preparing_candidate.

ajv's handling of OpenAPI 3.0 `nullable` and the exact per-case fixture outcomes are inferred from the recorded passing run (independentlyCheckedFixtures 38, exit 0) rather than from executing the validator myself.

The packaged access-policy consumer's behavior is known only from its exit code and the absence of stdout; the example asserts one offline round-trip (examples/access_policies.rs:49) and otherwise discards results, so its execution proves compilation and a clean run against the extracted archive, not deep behavioral coverage.

I judged phase 17 only. Phases 1-16 artifacts, prior release evidence and historical CI/packaging infrastructure were treated as historical context, not as acceptance for this source; the 'planned'/experimental live status of the five new endpoints is a recorded scope limitation of this phase, not a missing deliverable.
